thesis: Centene Corporation (NYSE: CNC) is the largest U.S. Medicaid and Health Insurance Marketplace insurer and a major Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plan administrator. **[Fact]** The company collects premiums and capitated payments from state Medicaid agencies, the federal Medicare program, and individual Marketplace customers, then pays medical claims and earns a spread on medical management, pharmacy, and administrative services. **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated revenue was **$194.8 billion**; normalized owner earnings (cash from operations minus capital spending) were **$4.3 billion** on **$5.1 billion** of operating cash flow. **[Fact]** Reportable segments are Medicaid, Medicare, Commercial (Marketplace and employer), and Other. **[Inference]** The equity is a scaled managed-care compounder on government-program cash flows, but earnings quality is dominated by medical-cost trend, Medicaid redeterminations, and periodic goodwill charges rather than hidden assets.
why_market_wrong: The market may be treating the **FY2025 net loss of $6.7 billion** (driven by a **$6.7 billion** goodwill impairment on Magellan Health) as a permanent cash-flow impairment, while underweighting **normalized owner earnings near $4.3 billion**, **$24.2 billion** of cash at mid-2026, and a share price **36% below** our base intrinsic value per share. **[Inference]** Return is not a dated catalyst story; it is **earnings power at a discount** if medical-cost trend stabilizes after Medicaid redeterminations and Marketplace mix shifts. **[Opinion]** The inefficiency is headline risk on reported losses and Medicaid membership volatility, not an undisclosed asset mark.
